subject: Security review language: audit events + retention for model metadata changes
body:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 8:30 AM PST
Subject: Security review language: audit events + retention for model metadata changes

Team — following up from the FinchBank security review (and SUP-18421). They’re asking for very specific language on:

1) What audit events we generate for model metadata changes + customer-visible changelog publication
2) Retention/immutability guarantees (and whether customers can export to SIEM)

I’m attaching the questionnaire and a draft field mapping I put together. Can you sanity check and help me land on wording we can reuse across reviews?

Questions we need to answer cleanly:
- Do we log CREATE/UPDATE/DEPRECATE model version metadata, plus “publish release note” actions?
- Do audit events include actor identity + timestamp + before/after or diff?
- How long do we retain by default vs enterprise? Can we commit to a number (e.g., 1 year / 7 years) without overpromising?

If we can align by EOD, I can send FinchBank a consolidated response tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Ava
—
Ava Chen
Security & Compliance (Customer Assurance)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: FinchBank_Security_Questionnaire_v3.2.xlsx
Attachment: audit-event-field-mapping_draft_v0.4.pdf


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 9:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Security review language: audit events + retention for model metadata changes

Yes, we should answer “yes” on the event coverage, with careful scoping.

What we can commit to (current plan + aligns with the audit logging spec draft):
- Events for model metadata: create, update, deprecate/restore (if allowed), and any field-level changes within the schema.
- Events for customer-visible notes: draft created, moved to in_review, publish, supersede/rollback (correction), and access-control changes to who can publish.

Data included:
- event_id (unique)
- timestamp
- actor (internal user/service principal) + auth context
- object identifiers (model_id, version_id)
- action type
- changed_fields list + previous/new values OR a diff blob (we should say “field-level diff” rather than “full before/after record”)
- request_id / trace_id for correlation

We should NOT claim:
- “immutable/WORM” unless Kevin confirms the storage/controls. We can say “tamper-evident” if we’re doing signed event payloads / append-only semantics.

I’ll let Kevin speak to retention + immutability controls.

-Marcus


From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 10:11 AM PST
Subject: Re: Security review language: audit events + retention for model metadata changes

Agree with Marcus. On retention/immutability, here’s what’s safe to say today vs what’s roadmap:

Retention (safe language):
- Audit events for the control plane are retained for a minimum of 12 months.
- Longer retention is available for enterprise customers by contract (we’ve been using 24 months and 7 years as options in other areas, but we should confirm what Legal is comfortable committing to for this specific stream).

Immutability / tamper evidence:
- We can say “append-only audit log with restricted write access” and “changes to published changelog entries are recorded as new events (supersede/correct) rather than in-place edits.”
- If FinchBank asks for cryptographic immutability: we should say “tamper-evident controls are in progress” unless we’ve already shipped signing + verification. Right now the design is to sign event payloads and store hashes to detect modification, but not GA yet.

Export:
- We can say we support export via API and can provide logs in a structured format for ingestion into common SIEMs.
- If they ask for native Splunk/QRadar connector: not yet (we’d phrase as “via customer-managed ingestion from our export endpoints”).

If helpful, I can give you a paragraph you can drop directly into the questionnaire once Olga weighs in on the exact retention phrasing.

-Kevin


From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 11:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Security review language: audit events + retention for model metadata changes

+1 to keeping the language tight and verifiable.

For enterprise questionnaires, I suggest we standardize on:
- “Minimum 12 months retention for audit logs” (no “at least” / no open-ended)
- “Extended retention available contractually” (don’t name 7 years unless it’s explicitly in the MSA/SOW we’re negotiating)

If FinchBank requires a number for extended retention:
- We can say: “We support extended retention terms; exact retention duration is defined in the customer agreement.”

Also, for regulated customers, they often ask about access controls:
- Mention RBAC for who can edit metadata and separate RBAC for who can approve/publish customer-visible notes.
- Mention that audit logs include the identity of the actor and the action performed.

I can review the exact answer text before you send if you paste it here.

Olga
GRC


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 12:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Security review language: audit events + retention for model metadata changes

One more nuance for the “who can change what” section (FinchBank asked this verbally on 2/11):

- Model metadata edits are restricted to a small set of internal roles (Model Catalog / Release Eng) and enforced via centralized authorization.
- Publication of customer-visible release notes requires approval (draft -> in_review -> published), and publish permissions are narrower than edit permissions.
- Emergency corrections do not overwrite prior published notes; they create a superseding entry and preserve the original for audit.

If you want, I can provide a one-sentence statement about separation of duties (edit vs publish) that tends to land well with procurement/security.

Naomi
Compliance Product Review


From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 2:12 PM PST
Subject: Re: Security review language: audit events + retention for model metadata changes

Thanks all — here’s the draft response I’m planning to send (please reply inline with edits).

---
AUDIT EVENTS
Redwood maintains audit logs for administrative actions related to model metadata and customer-visible model release notes. Logged events include creation and updates of model/version metadata, deprecation actions, and release note workflow actions (draft, review, publish, and correction via superseding entries). Audit events record the action performed, timestamp, actor identity, affected model/version identifiers, and field-level change details, and include correlation identifiers (e.g., request_id/trace_id) for investigation.

ACCESS CONTROLS
Access to edit model metadata and to approve/publish customer-visible release notes is controlled via role-based access control (RBAC). Publish/approval permissions are more restrictive than edit permissions, supporting separation of duties.

RETENTION / IMMUTABILITY
Audit events are retained for a minimum of 12 months. Extended retention is available contractually for enterprise customers. Published release notes are not modified in place; corrections are issued as new superseding entries to preserve history.

EXPORT
Audit logs can be exported in a structured format via API for ingestion into customer-managed logging/SIEM systems.
---

If this looks good, I’ll send to FinchBank + close the loop on SUP-18421 tomorrow AM.

Ava
